summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for abdominal pain, headaches, and generalized body pain. Evaluation revealed no acute abdominal pathology on ultrasound, and labs showed stable renal function with mild metabolic acidosis. Abdominal pain was attributed to constipation and gastroparesis, supported by lack of bowel movement for over a week and a reassuring physical exam. She was treated with an intensified bowel regimen including Miralax, lactulose, and a soap suds enema, which resulted in a bowel movement. Peritoneal dialysis was performed to address accumulated uremic symptoms. Her migraines and fibromyalgia pain were managed with home medications and improved during the stay. A MOLST form was completed at her request for DNR/DNI status. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up planned with her PCP and gastroenterologist.
problems: Type 1 diabetes mellitus with diabetic autonomic (poly)neuropathy
Migraine, unspecified, not intractable, without status migrainosus
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
